premises.text: Mobile app development is hard, expensive, and slow because it requires many languages, technologies, and frameworks
premises.evidence_span: mobile application development is hard. It requires knowledge of many programming languages, technologies, and frameworks

premises.text: A PowerPoint-like drag-and-drop editor with a component library lets non-technical users build flexible custom mobile apps
premises.evidence_span: a non-technical user can drag and drop components and build their own awesome mobile app

premises.text: Apps built on the platform are native for best look, feel, and performance
premises.evidence_span: the apps that are built are native

premises.text: A live preview app lets builders test and interact on a mobile device while editing
premises.evidence_span: we have a preview app. This allows you to test and interact with the application as you're building it live on your mobile device

premises.text: The product sits between developer tools and rigid template builders by combining template simplicity with full customization
premises.evidence_span: We have the simplicity of templates, but you can customize the app in every single way

premises.text: Future platform extension will let third-party developers build blocks with a marketplace, like WordPress for mobile
premises.evidence_span: in the future, we'll extend it to other developers to build on top of our platform

value.text: Non-technical users can build flexible native mobile apps as easily as PowerPoint
value.evidence_span: What if building mobile apps was as easy as PowerPoint

causal_links.evidence_span: We believe that App Architect is a solution to that problem
if you can build a PowerPoint slide deck, you too can become a mobile app developer
we see ourselves. as WordPress for mobile

notes: Demo component cascade (map, RSS, gallery, social buttons) folded into the drag-and-drop editor mechanism (§4.1.7). Native output and live preview split as separately claimed product conditions with own contribution to value. Cost/time figures kept as quantitative detail of the hard-development pain (§4.1). Market-size vision framing largely excluded; WordPress/marketplace treated as asserted future platform module. Singleton D1/D3 retained. Anti-template: problem, builder product, and platform extension separately revisable.
